primary_location: Jerusalem, Jordan Valley, Judean Desert, Coastal Plain
severity_metric: 41.5°C in Jerusalem; 47.8°C in Jordan Valley; 5-day duration
tectonic_or_synoptic_driver: Persistent upper-level anticyclonic ridge ('heat dome') causing strong atmospheric subsidence and easterly desert advection from the Arabian desert.
summary: An extraordinarily intense early summer heatwave broke multiple June temperature records across Israel. In Jerusalem, mountain temperatures exceeded 41°C, placing extreme strain on healthcare facilities and electrical grids, while igniting several brushfires along the Jerusalem transport corridor.
emergency_response_and_recovery: Ministry of Health and Magen David Adom issued national high-risk heat advisories; Israel Electric Corporation managed emergency reserve capacity; municipal cooling centers opened in Jerusalem.
sources: Israel Meteorological Service (IMS) Climate Monitoring Division (June 2024) | Jerusalem Institute for Policy Research (JIPR) Urban Heat Island Study | Magen David Adom Emergency Statistics Summary | ThinkHazard! Extreme Heat Hazard Assessment

event_name: June 2024 Mecca Extreme Heat Wave Disaster (Hajj 1445 AH)
primary_location: Mecca, Mina, Mount Arafat, Muzdalifah
severity_metric: 51.8°C (125.2°F) at Grand Mosque / 1,301 heat-related fatalities
tectonic_or_synoptic_driver: Extreme subtropical anticyclone dome over the Arabian Peninsula creating suffocating adiabatic heating.
summary: Historic extreme heatwave coinciding with the 2024 Hajj pilgrimage. Surface temperatures at the Great Mosque reached 51.8°C (125.2°F). Hundreds of unregistered pilgrims walking long distances without air-conditioned shelter suffered fatal heatstrokes.
emergency_response_and_recovery: Saudi Ministry of Health deployed over 6,500 heat-exhaustion hospital beds, massive misting towers, and dispatched emergency cooling ambulances.
sources: Saudi Ministry of Health Official Statement (June 2024) | National Center for Meteorology (NCM) | World Meteorological Organization (WMO) Heat Registry

event_name: November 2024 Southern Coastal & Ashdod Floods (שיטפונות מישור החוף הדרומי 2024)
primary_location: Ashdod, Ashkelon, Yavne Coastal Strip
severity_metric: 92 mm in 3 hours / Route 4 underpasses flooded
tectonic_or_synoptic_driver: Stationary coastal trough drawing deep Mediterranean marine moisture into a concentrated convergence line.
summary: Severe autumn downpour in November 2024 over Ashdod and Ashkelon. Localized flooding inundated urban thoroughfares, submerged major underpasses on Highway 4, and damaged dozens of commercial ground-floor properties.
emergency_response_and_recovery: Municipal pump crews deployed mobile drainage pumps; police closed low-lying interchanges until waters receded.
sources: Israel Meteorological Service Precipitation Annals Nov 2024 | Ashdod Municipal Drainage Authority | Israel Police Traffic Directorate

event_name: April 2025 Judaean Mountains Wildfires (שריפות הרי יהודה 2025)
primary_location: Judaean Mountains, Jerusalem Corridor, Neve Shalom, Beko'a, Ta'oz, Mevo Horon
severity_metric: 25,000 Dunams Burned / 45+ Injured / 100+ Fire Ignitions
tectonic_or_synoptic_driver: Record-breaking early spring Sharav with temperatures >38°C, relative humidity under 10%, and extreme easterly gusts sweeping through dried Judean pine forest fuels.
summary: Massive wildfire outbreak spanning over 100 separate fires across the Judaean Mountains west of Jerusalem. Declared a national emergency, requiring IDF ground troops, bulldozers, dozens of firefighting aircraft, and international mutual assistance requests.
emergency_response_and_recovery: National state of emergency declared; IDF Home Front Command and Combat Engineering Corps deployed; over 10,000 residents evacuated from mountain communities; international firefighting aircraft requested from Mediterranean neighbors.
sources: Israel Fire and Rescue Authority Operational Summary Report (May 2025) | Israel Meteorological Service (IMS Sharav & Fire Risk Assessment) | Jerusalem Institute for Policy Research (JIPR Urban Resilience) | Nature and Parks Authority

event_name: August 2025 Record-Breaking Subtropical Heat Dome (גל החום הכבד באוגוסט 2025)
disaster_subtype: Persistent Subtropical Heat Dome & Heavy Sharav
primary_location: Jerusalem, Judean Foothills, Jordan Rift Valley, Coastal Plain
severity_metric: 41.3°C in Jerusalem / 48.5°C in Jordan Valley / FWI > 60
tectonic_or_synoptic_driver: Extremely persistent high-pressure subtropical ridge (heat dome) parked over the Levant, causing severe adiabatic compression and record-breaking thermal anomalies.
summary: Historic multi-day heatwave in August 2025 breaking monthly temperature records across Jerusalem and Israel. Ambient temperatures exceeded 41°C in the Jerusalem mountains and 48°C in the Dead Sea basin, stressing lifelines and triggering severe wildfire bans.
emergency_response_and_recovery: Ministry of Health issued national Code Red thermal warning; Magen David Adom placed all ambulance crews on maximum alert; municipal water misting stations deployed across Jerusalem city center.
sources: Israel Meteorological Service (IMS) Monthly Climate Review (August 2025) | Ministry of Health Epidemiological Surveillance Division | Jerusalem Institute for Policy Research (JIPR) Climate Resilience Report

event_name: Dead Sea Basin Sinkholes Hazard (Continuous Crisis)
primary_location: Dead Sea Western Shore (Ein Gedi, Mineral Beach, Ein Bokek)
severity_metric: > 7,000 Sinkholes / 1.2 m/yr Sea Level Drop
tectonic_or_synoptic_driver: Anthropogenic diversion of Jordan River waters causing the Dead Sea level to fall by > 1.2 meters per year; subsurface fresh groundwater dissolves subterranean salt beds, causing sudden cavern collapses.
summary: An ongoing geological crisis. Over 7,000 sinkholes have collapsed along the Dead Sea shoreline, swallowing agricultural date plantations, roads, and camping beaches.
emergency_response_and_recovery: Geological Survey of Israel (GSI) established real-time InSAR radar satellite monitoring and hazard zoning maps; Ministry of Transport spent hundreds of millions on bridge bypasses.
sources: Geological Survey of Israel (GSI Sinkhole Research Division) | University of Haifa - Department of Geography & NDI | Jerusalem Institute for Policy Research | Ministry of Environmental Protection

event_name: July 2026 Mediterranean Heat Dome & Grid Stress Crisis (גל חום יולי 2026)
disaster_subtype: Subtropical High Blocking & Heat Exhaustion Wave
primary_location: National, Jerusalem, Coastal Plain, Jordan Valley
severity_metric: 6 days >40°C in valleys / 39.5°C in Jerusalem / Peak electrical load
tectonic_or_synoptic_driver: Persistent upper-level anticyclonic heat dome over the Eastern Mediterranean producing intense adiabatic warming and stagnant air.
summary: Prolonged July 2026 heatwave shattering regional mid-summer records. Consecutive days exceeding 43°C in inland valleys and 39.5°C in Jerusalem stressed the national power grid to its all-time peak load (16,200 MW), causing rolling power outages and poultry agricultural die-offs.
emergency_response_and_recovery: Magen David Adom (MDA) treated hundreds of heatstroke cases; NEMA activated municipal cooling centers for senior citizens across Jerusalem and southern cities.
sources: Israel Meteorological Service Monthly Review July 2026 | Ministry of Health Epidemiological Heat Stroke Registry | NEMA Emergency Bulletin
